question: An engineer implements an Application Performance Monitoring (APM) solution. The solution runs in a vSphere infrastructure where the vSwitch support for promiscuous mode is disabled for security reasons. As a result, the final implementation must receive a copy of bidirectional traffic to a load balancer that is connected to a Cisco Nexus 93108 Series Switch. The APM solution supports GRE encapsulated traffic. Which configuration must be applied to the switch to meet this requirement?
options: interface vlan1 / switchport monitor / destination ip 10.1.1.1 / exit / monitor session 1 rx / monitor session 1 tx / source interface ethernet1/9
monitor session 1 both / source interface ethernet 1/9 / destination interface ethernet 1/12 / erspan-id 1 / vrf mgmt0 / filter vlan 3 / no shut
configure terminal / monitor session 1 type erspan-source / erspan-id 1 / destination ip 10.1.1.1 / source interface ethernet 1/9 both / vrf default / no shut
interface ethernet 1/9 / erspan-id 1 / monitor session 1 type erspan-source / interface mgmt0 / monitor session 1 type erspan-destination / destination ip 10.1.1.1 / no shut
theory: Because the vSwitch has promiscuous mode disabled, a virtual APM sensor can't simply sniff local traffic, so the copy of load-balancer traffic must instead be mirrored at the physical switch and delivered as a routed, GRE-encapsulated ERSPAN stream that the APM tool decapsulates remotely. Configuring an erspan-source session with the erspan-id, a destination IP address (since the copy must be routed off-box rather than sent to a local interface), the both direction on the monitored interface to capture inbound and outbound traffic, and a VRF for reachability is what produces a proper GRE/ERSPAN mirrored feed rather than a purely local SPAN copy. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — ERSPAN Source Sessions for Remote/Routed Traffic Capture)
